summary.text: One of the fifty daughters of Danaus by Crino — by lot the bride of Hippocorystes son of Egyptus when the sons of Aegyptus married the Danaids at Argos; distinct from Hyperippe daughter of Arcas, wife of Endymion in one Pausanias account.

story.text: Apollodorus lists Hyperippe fourth among the daughters of Danaus borne on Crino. When the youngest sons of Egyptus by Hephaestine cast lots, Hippocorystes drew Hyperippe. On the wedding night she received her father's dagger and, like her sisters, slew her bridegroom — Hyginus counts her among the brides who obeyed Danaus.
